title: Jungie Studio
description: A production-grade, single-vendor e-commerce storefront for an LA-based pottery brand. Every piece is one of a kind, so instead of a cart-and-checkout flow I built an email-based reservation system that holds a piece for one buyer. Serverless Next.js on AWS Lambda behind CloudFront, self-hosted auth with an admin back-office, and the entire cloud footprint provisioned as code with Terraform.
role: Solo Full-Stack Developer — Architecture, Frontend, Backend, Cloud Infrastructure, Auth & Email Deliverability
tech: AWS (Lambda, CloudFront, RDS, S3, SES, SNS, Route 53, ACM, VPC)

highlights.label: Architecture
highlights.title: Serverless Next.js on AWS Lambda
highlights.body: Built on the Next.js 15 App Router — React 19 Server Components and Server Actions, TypeScript end to end — packaged for AWS Lambda with OpenNext and served globally through CloudFront, with Origin Access Control locking the S3 origins.

highlights.label: Infrastructure
highlights.title: The whole cloud footprint as code
highlights.body: Terraform provisions every AWS resource — RDS Postgres, in-VPC Lambda, S3, CloudFront, Route 53, ACM, SES, and SNS — with least-privilege IAM scoped per resource and application secrets kept out of version control.

highlights.label: Data
highlights.title: Type-safe schema tuned for serverless
highlights.body: A normalized PostgreSQL 16 schema modeled in Drizzle ORM with type-safe queries and version-controlled migrations, connected via the postgres-js driver tuned for Lambda connection cycling (prepared statements disabled).

highlights.label: Commerce
highlights.title: Atomic reservations for one-of-a-kind inventory
highlights.body: Because every piece is unique, an atomic SELECT…FOR UPDATE inside a transaction stops two customers from reserving the same item. Zod validates each submission, and the buyer's payment preference is captured for out-of-band settlement — no cart or processor, by design.

highlights.label: Auth & security
highlights.title: Self-hosted auth with defense in depth
highlights.body: Better Auth (Drizzle adapter, Google OAuth) backs a role-gated admin back-office, re-checking session and role inside each Server Action and page rather than trusting middleware alone — the CVE-2025-29927 middleware-bypass lesson applied.

highlights.label: Deliverability
highlights.title: Production-grade email on SES
highlights.body: Owned end-to-end deliverability: DKIM signing, a custom MAIL FROM subdomain publishing SPF, a DMARC policy, and an SNS topic routing bounce/complaint events to keep rates within SES thresholds.

highlights.label: Cost engineering
highlights.title: A NAT trade-off that cut egress 8×
highlights.body: Routed private-subnet egress through a self-hosted fck-nat instance instead of a managed NAT Gateway, cutting that line item from ~$32/mo to ~$4/mo and holding the full always-on stack to ~$24–28/mo.

highlights.label: Developer experience
highlights.title: Reproducible local environment
highlights.body: Docker Compose runs Next.js and PostgreSQL as isolated services so the environment is reproducible and migrations run consistently from laptop to cloud.

highlights.label: Roadmap
highlights.title: Scheduled drops and AI assistance
highlights.body: Planned a scheduled 'drop' storefront — open only during drop windows, with RDS and NAT powered down between drops via EventBridge Scheduler to cut idle cost roughly 4× — plus rate-limited LLM integration for customer-facing product assistance.

title: WonResume AI
description: An AI resume-tailoring web app that turns a pasted job description into an ATS-scored, voice-preserving tailored resume and cover letter. A deterministic scoring engine and Claude-powered review grade each draft, editable per-bullet suggestions keep the candidate's own voice, and every application is versioned with a side-by-side diff — all behind Supabase auth with row-level security.
role: Solo Full-Stack Developer — Architecture, Frontend, Backend, AI Integration, Design System

highlights.label: Architecture
highlights.title: Full-stack Next.js on Vercel
highlights.body: A production app on the Next.js 16 App Router with React 19 Server Components, server actions, and TypeScript end to end, deployed on Vercel.

highlights.label: Data & security
highlights.title: Row-level security by default
highlights.body: A Supabase Postgres backend with row-level security on every table and cookie-based SSR auth, isolating each user's career data, resumes, and applications at the database layer.

highlights.label: Scoring
highlights.title: A deterministic ATS scoring engine
highlights.body: Formatting, keyword and JD coverage, impact, and language checks implemented as pure, testable functions that return sub-scores plus concrete fixes — no black-box AI for the parts that must be reproducible.

highlights.label: AI integration
highlights.title: Task-matched Claude models
highlights.body: The Anthropic Claude API is wired with task-based model selection — Haiku for fast extraction and parsing, Sonnet for tailoring, review, and cover letters — balancing latency against cost under an enforced monthly spend cap.

highlights.label: Reliability
highlights.title: Schema-validated LLM output
highlights.body: Zod schemas act as a strict validation contract for all model output, with null-tolerant coercion so malformed responses degrade gracefully instead of crashing the request.

highlights.label: Tailoring
highlights.title: Voice-preserving, per-bullet edits
highlights.body: Claude proposes per-bullet edits the user can accept, edit, or reject, capturing each decision to learn the candidate's writing voice while the score updates live.

highlights.label: Output
highlights.title: Pixel-consistent client-side PDFs
highlights.body: Resumes and cover letters render entirely client-side from a single shared react-pdf template, eliminating rendering drift between the live preview and the downloaded file.

highlights.label: Workflow
highlights.title: A versioned application pipeline
highlights.body: A drag-and-drop kanban board built on native HTML5 drag-and-drop with zero dependencies, optimistic updates that revert on failure, and an LCS-based diff to compare any two saved resume versions.

highlights.label: Design system
highlights.title: A cohesive, accessible surface
highlights.body: A reusable Tailwind v4 design system — CSS-first tokens, accessible UI primitives, and staggered entrance animations that respect prefers-reduced-motion — spanning the app and a public marketing landing page.

title: ₩on Stock
description: A personal stock research platform that automates equity analysis with AWS serverless infrastructure and LLM-powered document summarization. An event-driven pipeline ingests prices, news, SEC filings, and federal policy actions, then delivers a curated email newsletter every other day with quarterly narratives, watchlist snapshots, and policy impact analysis. On top of the same pipeline, a private Next.js dashboard on Vercel — backed by a cost-aware DynamoDB cache, Supabase auth, and a signed cross-cloud call into the AWS backend — adds live watchlist management, interactive price-history charts, and per-ticker deep dives.
role: Solo Developer — Architecture, Cloud Infrastructure, Backend, Full-Stack Dashboard, Prompt Engineering
tech: AWS (Lambda, DynamoDB, S3, EventBridge, SES, Athena)

highlights.label: Data pipeline
highlights.title: Five sources, one event-driven pipeline
highlights.body: An event-driven serverless architecture ingests, processes, and stores financial data from yfinance, Financial Modeling Prep, NewsAPI, SEC EDGAR, and the Federal Register API.

highlights.label: System design
highlights.title: A read-through cache that decouples traffic from API limits
highlights.body: A DynamoDB read-through cache, refreshed once daily by an EventBridge cron, serves every price-history chart and watchlist sparkline — so dashboard page views cost zero upstream calls and third-party API usage stays flat against a 250-request/day free-tier ceiling no matter how heavily the app is browsed.

highlights.label: Full-stack
highlights.title: A private dashboard spanning three clouds
highlights.body: A Next.js 14 App Router dashboard on Vercel — React Server Components and server actions, TypeScript end to end — securely invokes the AWS Lambda backend through the AWS SDK with scoped IAM credentials, while a Supabase Postgres read model with row-level security and Google OAuth backs the authenticated watchlist and holdings views.

highlights.label: Frontend
highlights.title: Server-rendered charts, tuned for cost and speed
highlights.body: Watchlist rows render sparklines as server-generated inline SVG — no per-row charting library or client JavaScript — while detail pages ship interactive Recharts price-history charts with range selection and an end-of-day 'as of' timestamp, spending client-side JS only where interaction earns it.

highlights.label: Intelligence
highlights.title: Model-matched LLM summarization
highlights.body: Amazon Bedrock summarizes 10-K filings, earnings calls, news, and policy actions — routing between Claude Sonnet and Haiku by task complexity to keep monthly Bedrock cost under $10.

highlights.label: Differentiator
highlights.title: Policy Watch for regulatory signals
highlights.body: A dedicated layer monitors executive orders and political news from the Federal Register, surfacing regulatory developments affecting tracked equities — a research angle absent from comparable retail platforms.

highlights.label: Infrastructure
highlights.title: Least-privilege, fully Terraformed
highlights.body: The entire stack is provisioned with Terraform using remote state in S3 with DynamoDB locking, per-Lambda IAM roles, and SSM Parameter Store for secret management.

highlights.label: Delivery
highlights.title: A stratified newsletter, every other day
highlights.body: Amazon SES delivers a layered digest: always-on sections like the market overview and watchlist snapshot, event-triggered earnings and 10-K primers, and a rotating AI deep-dive on individual tickers.

highlights.label: Prompt engineering
highlights.title: Factual by design
highlights.body: Version-controlled prompts are engineered for factual, unbiased extraction — explicitly avoiding buy/sell recommendations or predictive language — to support long-horizon investment research.
